Face concentration — dual-density Voronoi (dense face, coarse background)

Base config: signed-damage dw=0.5 cw=0.5 agree=0.90 (confirmed active). Gate metric: corrected colour-match ≤0.30 vs the original source (not the old coverage rate) — both arms below sit at ~52-53%. Source: oil painting (Vermeer girl, background removed).

The matched test (same ~217 shards, 6 seeds)

Look at the face crops: uniform (blobby) → concentrated (slightly finer, a bit more eye/cheek structure) → 2750 shards (features genuinely resolve). Concentration helps a little at the same budget; only ~9× the shard budget actually resolves the face.

Verdict

  • Face concentration is REAL, not noise — +0.013 faceSSIM beyond the seed stdev. This is the FIRST lever in the whole search to beat the control on the face at all.
  • The mechanism matters: dense-face seeding works where the earlier semantic mask (cap-shrinking only) was pure noise (+0.004). Same idea, stronger implementation, real effect.
  • But it is marginal and visually imperceptible (0.524→0.537, ~2.5%). It does NOT resolve the face at 300 shards. The binding limit is the shard budget (~2750 needed), which is fabrication, not algorithm — colour-match reproduction stays ~52% either way.
  • The other five axes stay saturated on face recognizability (established across prior runs), so I did not burn the full 6-axis sweep to re-confirm that. Concentration is the only real lever and it is small.

The density sweep it came from

Progressive concentration (face9 → face40) at ≤300 total: the face crop sharpens gradually. Real, gradual, and small.

Bottom line (unchanged, now with a small caveat)

At a 300-shard budget, no configuration — including dense face concentration — produces a recognizable oil-painting face. Concentration is a real but imperceptible improvement. For a 300-shard build: use posterised/flat sources (which read at ~30-80 shards). If the budget ever rises, dense-face concentration is now implemented and gives a free (if small) boost.
